solution_metadata.competition: Flavours of Physics: Finding tau to 3mu
solution_metadata.team: Tatiana Likhomanenko & Alexey Rogozhnikov (Yandex Data School)
solution_metadata.source_license: NO LICENSE (blocked for ingestion; hep_ml is Apache-2.0)

evidence_summary.gap_reason: Domain-specific feature selection based on physics knowledge of mass-independent variables. Not a reusable atom -- the 'safe' feature set is specific to this particle physics problem.

Training-time decorrelation via modified loss function (BinFlatnessLossFunction). Core algorithm lives in hep_ml (Apache 2.0). Generalizes to any fairness-aware ML scenario. High-value ingestion target but solution repo has no license -- must use hep_ml or reimplement from arXiv:1410.4140.
Post-hoc noise injection for constraint satisfaction. Simple (one line of code) but the insight that noise_level=0.40 optimally trades AUC for KS compliance is valuable. No matching atom.

KS agreement test between real and simulated data using ROC-curve machinery. Generalizes to domain adaptation / covariate shift detection. Solution repo has no license but algorithm is standard KS test with a clever implementation.

CvM statistic for prediction-protected variable independence. Rolling window over sorted mass with rank-based CDF comparison. Generalizes to any fairness auditing scenario. Must reimplement from standard CvM definition due to no license.

Segment-weighted ROC AUC with emphasis on low-TPR region. Generalizes to any scenario where certain operating points matter more. No matching atom -- sklearn's partial AUC is related but different (single segment, not weighted segments).

architect_test_expectations.description: All 6 stages are gaps. This CDG tests the architect's handling of constraint gates (KS, CvM) that act as hard pass/fail filters before metric computation.
architect_test_expectations.critical_finding: The constraint-gate pattern (hard statistical tests as acceptance criteria) is broadly applicable to fairness-aware ML. The architect should recognize that compute_ks_agreement and compute_cvm_mass_decorrelation are evaluation/auditing atoms, not model components. The NO LICENSE status blocks direct ingestion but clean-room reimplementation from papers is feasible for all atoms.
architect_test_expectations.expected_retrieval_path: No atoms should be found. All stages should be reported as gaps. The flatness_constrained_gradient_boosting atom may be partially matchable to hep_ml (Apache 2.0) if that library is indexed.
